data.long_meaning: The name Sharovind is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Shara' meaning king and 'Vind' meaning love. It signifies a king who embodies the essence of love and joy. The name Sharovind carries the meaning “King of Love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharovind usually hope their child will grow to embody king of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Sharovind holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism as it represents the divine king of love. It signifies the power of love and joy in one's life and is believed to bring happiness and prosperity.
data.etymology: Sharovind belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of Love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharovind total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

historical_references.reference: Sharovind is an alternate name for the Hindu deity Sharavanabhagavan, who is also known as Khandoba, a form of the god Shiva popular in Maharashtra, India. Sharavanabhagavan is believed to be the protector of the downtrodden and the god of relief from suffering. This name gained popularity during the Maratha Empire, a historical Hindu kingdom in India that existed from the 14th to the 18th centuries.

Another reference suggests that Sharovind may be an alternate name for the Hindu god Shiva, particularly in the context of the Sharovar Temple located in the Indian state of Maharashtra. The temple is believed to have originated during the Chalukya Dynasty (543-1189 AD) and is one of the oldest temples dedicated to Shiva in the region.
